mappings.note: Sorts the three organs of government from a non-organ. Constitutional structure under the goal.

The 73rd Amendment bringing Panchayati Raj into the Constitution is about the local tier of government, which is LO-201's subject. Not the bare goal, because local self-government has its own outcome.
Directive Principles as guidance for the state rather than enforceable rules. Constitutional structure under the goal.
How the number of Parts and Schedules has grown since 1950. A fact about the document, so the goal.
Matches constitutional ideas to the countries that inspired them. Sources of the Constitution under the goal.
Matches Preamble values such as fraternity and liberty to their meanings. Several values are in play, so the goal rather than the equality outcome alone.
Names the constitution as the document of basic principles and laws. The goal's own subject.
The helium-filled case in which the original is kept. A fact about the document.
Republic Day as the date the Constitution came into force. Constitutional history under the goal.
Names one organ of government. Constitutional structure under the goal.
Names the Constituent Assembly formed in 1946. The drafting process, so the goal.
Names the Chairman of the Constituent Assembly. A drafting-process recall.
Names the Chairman of the Drafting Committee. Same drafting-process lane.
What Article 14's Right to Equality guarantees - equality before the law and equal protection. The equality outcome stated directly.
The Fundamental Duty to value and preserve composite culture. Constitutional duties under the goal.
What the demanding amendment process signifies about the Constitution. Constitutional process under the goal.

Free and compulsory schooling for six to fourteen year-olds matched to its constitutional provision. A specific right under the goal; equality of opportunity is implied but the item asks which provision.
Sorts real influences on the Constitution from a false one. Sources of the Constitution under the goal.
The Assembly's original membership before Partition. A drafting-process fact.
Rejects the claim that Fundamental Rights are absolute and unrestricted. Constitutional structure under the goal.
Completes separation of powers with the judiciary interpreting law. A constitutional principle under the goal.
The executive's role in a parliamentary democracy. An organ of government under the goal.
The date the Assembly finished drafting. Constitutional history under the goal.
Rajendra Prasad on respect for others' views and the capacity for compromise as qualities a constitution needs. Constitutional values under the goal.
Sorts genuine influences on the Constitution from hereditary monarchy. Sources of the Constitution under the goal.
Checks and balances stopping any organ becoming too powerful. A constitutional principle under the goal.
'Equality of status and of opportunity' in the Preamble and what it aims to secure. The equality outcome, not the general goal.
The size of the Drafting Committee. A drafting-process fact under the goal.
Constitutional commitment to heritage and to 'sarve bhavantu sukhinah' tied to India's civilisational values. Constitutional values under the goal.
A peaceful protest reflecting the Preamble's promise of liberty of thought, expression and action. The value at issue is liberty, so the goal rather than LO-198.
The three-tier structure of central, state and local self-government. The item rests on distinguishing the local tier from the others, which is LO-201.
Matches the original illustrations to the Parts they head, with one wrong pairing. A fact about the document, so the goal.
Rejects the claim that Fundamental Duties were in the 1950 text. Constitutional history under the goal.
The 1976 addition of 'socialist' and 'secular' to the Preamble. Constitutional history under the goal.
Rights meant for immediate enforcement against principles meant as long-term goals. Constitutional structure under the goal.
The freedom struggle's ideals feeding into the Constitution. Sources of constitutional values under the goal; equality is only one item in the list.
What adding Fundamental Duties says about citizenship - that rights come with responsibilities. Constitutional values under the goal.
A citizen blocked from assembling and speaking out - the right infringed is freedom of expression and assembly, a liberty rather than an equality question, so the goal.
The Constitution as supreme law because all three organs draw their powers from it. Constitutional supremacy under the goal.
The executive implementing laws against the legislature making them. Organs of government under the goal.
